Mutually exclusive cut strategy sources are covered at the Analyzer configuration boundary rather than standalone command argument parsing.

MMPDB-style one-cut product application min-pairs filtering and explicit hydrogen deletion boundary are covered; constant/query derivation subqueries selected-pair columns output/header/gzip multiprocessing and explain remain Phase 14 or Phase 15 workflow work.
RDKit FragmentMol tests 1 through 9 have OEMMPA analogs or accepted API-shape divergences based on structured fragment records.

Single-cut baseline and up-enumerated stereo records are compared row for row against a committed mmpdb 3.1.4 oracle. mmpdb keys its dedupe on attachment_order.variable_smiles.constant_smiles without the enumeration label, which restores the rows its frag1_indices reference defect would otherwise suppress, so that defect is unobservable at one cut.

Potential-stereocentre detection is exercised indirectly through the fixture: centres that survive a cut, a specified tag that is not a real centre and collapses to one achiral form, and prochiral carbons that a cut desymmetrises into new centres.

Carbon created-stereocentre up-enumeration matches mmpdb for every enumerating fixture structure. OEMMPA additionally enumerates three-coordinate nitrogen with no hydrogens, which mmpdb is_potential_chiral_center excludes, so N,N-dialkylamine and N,N-dialkylsulfonamide motifs are deliberately outside this fixture and remain an open divergence.

Ring-constrained and exocyclic E/Z geometry is verified against the oracle. Acyclic stereogenic double bonds are out of fixture scope: mmpdb asymmetric begin/end bond-direction transfer inverts exactly one of the two cuts flanking such a bond, and RDKit FragmentOnBonds agrees with OEMMPA rather than mmpdb there, so an acyclic case would pin an upstream error.

Explicit design difference. The mmpdb fragment command never produces hydrogen fragmentations; only transform and predict call this surface. The committed oracle therefore contains none, and a test pins the absence so it cannot become an unnoticed coverage gap.
